Home server configuration — OLDSRV (bare-metal Debian + Docker, RX 7600, 48 GB RAM)
=== Service placement (HD-135 split, 2026-08-18) ===
Old-srv keeps the GPU / LAN / storage-bound core (immich-ml, jellyfin,
sunshine, media/*arr, DNS, ha-standby) + the thin Alloy collector (dozzle moved to VPS, HD-135b).
The public edge + live-data apps + AI stack + observability backend + alert brain
(n8n) + backup agents moved to the VPS (group_vars/vps.yml). See docs/services.md.
Reachability (HD-397, decided 2026-09-19): oldsrv sits behind the home NAT, so a runner
that is not LAN-attached reaches it ONLY via the VPS jump. The jump therefore travels IN
THE INVENTORY (group var = every play sees it: home_servers.yml, all.yml, dns-seed.yml,
nut-deploy.yml, monitoring) instead of a per-command flag or one laptop's ssh alias —
same doctrine as playbooks/spark.yml ("keep it here so ANY runner converges spark").
From a LAN-attached runner it is a harmless no-op. The leg is the HOME leg (VLAN 10,
host_vars ansible_host): the Mgmt plane is sealed from the tunnel on purpose (HD-398 →
decision A). Matrix + the laptop alias contract: docs/network-vpn.md §Reaching LAN nodes
when away. (Measured 2026-09-19: because this var is passed on the ssh command line, no
`Host <ip>` block is needed for a converge — the per-IP blocks in the contract are for
scp/rsync/git and for humans who type an address.)
HA container pin (HD-192/HD-39): the PRIMARY (Pi, raspberry_pi.yml) and the
STANDBY (this host) MUST run the same version for clean manual failover. The
standby compose renders ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:{{ home_assistant_version }}
(standby.yml / home-assistant-standby template) — undefined here caused the
standby render to fail on oldsrv (2026-09-08). Keep in sync with raspberry_pi.yml.
AMD ROCm host userspace (roles/amd_rocm, docs/hardware-gpu.md)
HD-318 (2026-09-07): Ubuntu-noble AMD repo INCOMPATIBLE with Debian trixie
(rocm-cmake/hipcc dep conflicts). External AMD repo REMOVED — Debian trixie ships
rocm-opencl-icd/hipcc/rocminfo in main. Host userland = tooling/inspection only;
GPU containers bundle their own ROCm (immich-ml; ollama disabled 2026-09-07).
Home Assistant failover (docs/smart-home-failover.md)
ha_vip / ha_vip_cidr are defined once in group_vars/all.yml (SSOT).
n8n webhook for ha-failover.sh notifications (event/status payload). Empty = skip
notify (always journald-logged). Set once the n8n workflow exists (observability.md).
Failover trigger API (HD-17) — Homepage buttons call this endpoint on oldsrv.
Shared trigger token comes from 1Password `ha-failover_api` (api → credential),

Observability alerting (docs/observability.md) — Grafana alert email recipient.
SMTP fail-safe contact point in the monitoring role (grafana-contactpoints.yml.j2).
Decision HD-54 (Option B): dedicated transactional relay — SMTP2Go (mail-eu.smtp2go.com:2525).
Credentials: smtp_login (Login) in 1Password — the address (domen@kogler.si)
is the Grafana recipient; SMTP2Go authenticates with a separate SMTP username+password.
Host/port derive from the SMTP2Go connection SSOT in group_vars/all.yml (smtp2go_*).
n8n alert webhook — Grafana contact point posts here (monitoring role).
The n8n workflow 'homelab-alerts' on this route must exist before the first
alert (created at n8n setup; URL is internal, traefik-public network).
PrivadoVPN WireGuard egress for the qbittorrent gluetun sidecar (HD-318c).
SSOT for the NON-secret endpoint config of the VPN tunnel; gluetun runs the
provider in `custom` WireGuard mode (gluetun dropped the native `privado`
provider — HD-318c) so these values are supplied explicitly instead of via
a `SERVER_COUNTRIES`/`privado` server pick. The client private key is the

Source of the values: the PrivadoVPN WireGuard config handed over by the owner.
Spec: docs/services-downloads.md §VPN & Ingress.

egress through the tunnel; not rendered as a separate env.

--- Homelable (HD-45, re-scoped 2026-09-09): network/rack topology visualizer ---
Internal-only dashboard on OLDSRV (Home VLAN 10). Scanner target ranges + knobs;
the compose template (docker_services/homelable/) renders these into the backend env.
`homelable_scanner_ranges_json` = the VLAN subnets the nmap discovery sweeps (site
SSOT, network_ranges above), as a JSON-array STRING (Homelable reads SCANNER_RANGES as
a JSON env var — the compose env value is a string; keep it JSON-quoted). Keep scans
scoped to the LAN the owner curates; do NOT scan the modem-LAN / WAN. The owner approves
discovered devices into the canvas (Homelable Pending-Devices queue) — never auto-adds.
Live healthcheck poll interval (seconds) Homelable uses for every node's check method.
Optional deep-scan JSON port list (SCANNER_HTTP_RANGES, service-ID probes). Empty = off.
Only enable when a custom-port device is missed (e.g. '["9000-9100"]').
MCP sub-container (AI-tool topology read/write). OFF by default — the canvas is
curated first; turn on after the topology is populated + the owner approves AI write
(needs the homelable_mcp 1P item + a tailnet Pattern-A route for remote AI clients).
--- Pinned-AI tier on the RX 7600 (HD-391, decision #27: ggml/Vulkan) ---
Ports are INTERNAL to the `llm-backend` bridge — none of these legs is published on the
host (HD-59: the APIs have no auth, so the network is the boundary). They exist so a
consumer URL is stable and greppable.
Memory caps are HARD CAPS in the spark-dcgm doctrine (HD-379): measured peak, then
headroom, so a leak in one leg can never eat the card the whole tier shares with
immich-ML (3-5 GB during a job) and Jellyfin/Sunshine.
Plan of record + every measured number: docs/services-ai.md §3a.
Context window for BOTH GGUF legs. llama.cpp truncates SILENTLY beyond it and
llama-server's own default is 512 - which would slice a real ingest chunk in half. The RAG
ingest spec is token-based 512/64 (docs/services-ai.md §5b), so 2048 = that spec with 4x
headroom (bge-m3 supports 8192; paying KV memory for chunks that do not exist yet buys
nothing). Re-derive when rag-mcp (HD-268b) goes live and a real chunk size is measurable.
Physical batch/ubatch size (HD-391, measured live 2026-09-19): ctx-size alone is NOT enough.
The embedding endpoint rejects an input larger than the **ubatch**, and llama-server's error
message calls it "batch size" - which is why the first fix attempt (batch 2048, ubatch 512)
still answered HTTP 500 "input (842 tokens) is too large to process (current batch size: 512)",
because 512 was the Ubatch. So ubatch = batch = ctx: a 512-token ingest chunk plus its special
tokens must fit in one ubatch pass. VRAM consequence measured below (compute buffers scale with
ubatch, not with ctx) - see docs/services-ai.md §3a-1 for the before/after numbers.
EXPLICITLY an empty LIST, not a key-with-only-comments: YAML would parse that as None
and `litellm_scoped_keys | default([])` does NOT rescue None (the default filter fires on
UNDEFINED only) — `roles/docker_services/tasks/main.yml` op_derive_glue and
`tasks/deploy-service.yml` both pipe it through `map(attribute='vault_item')` and would
die on a full oldsrv converge. `[]` keeps those pipes clean.
VPS host configuration — netcup RS 2000 G12 (bought 2026-08-18, HD-93/HD-40B)
Replaces the earlier planned Contabo Storage VPS 30. Plain Debian root server with
Docker CE — the VPS is NOT a Proxmox node (no proxmox_bridges here, see home
`proxmox` role / homelab_mode). Host identity facts live here; billing lives in
`subscriptions.yml` (cost, renewal, status).
Grafana SMTP relay (HD-241 companion fix 2026-09-08): the VPS is its own group (not home_servers),
so the home_servers.yml `grafana_smtp_host` never applied — VPS Grafana fell back to `localhost:25`
(dead). Derive from the smtp2go SSOT (2525) so VPS Grafana can send alerts/emails.

HD-135b follow-up (tailnet-only dashboards): the tailnet Traefik edge (traefik-tailnet)
is served on the headscale sidecar node `vps-obs` (tag:sidecar). headscale
`dns.extra_records` maps the clean subdomain names (stats/logs/csui/traefik/auto
AND their *.ts.kogler.si twins) to this node's tailnet IPv4.
Tailnet IPv4s are assigned SEQUENTIALLY by headscale at node join — current known
nodes: 100.64.0.3 laptop, 100.64.0.4 phone. This value is filled at deploy time from
`headscale nodes list` after the sidecar joins (empty → headscale renders no

HD-268c (2026-08-29): Pattern-A tailnet sidecar IPs (vps-dsh / vps-pi-dev).
HD-355 (2026-09-10): the sidecars are REMOVED (dsh/pi-dev moved to oldsrv) —
these are now retained as historical/no-op values: the clean-URL DNS still
resolves to the edge (tailnet_sidecar_ip), and the edge reaches the backends
over WG to {{ oldsrv_home_ip }}:3080/:8080 (NOT via these sidecar IPs). They
stay only so any dangling config that references them resolves; do NOT rely on
them for routing.
Subdomains served by the tailnet edge (watched by headscale config.yaml.j2
extra_records render). Each entry is `{name: <sub>, ip: <tailnet IPv4>}`.
`ip` defaults to `tailnet_sidecar_ip` (the traefik-tailnet observability
edge on `vps-obs`, 100.64.0.1) when omitted. HD-297 (2026-08-31): EVERY
clean-URL FQDN (incl. dsh/pi) must resolve to this edge — it terminates TLS
(wildcard cert) + Host-routes to the backends. Do NOT pin the Pattern-A
sidecar IPs here: the sidecars only serve plain HTTP (:3080/:8080) with no
TLS/Host-routing, so pointing the FQDN at them breaks the clean URLs.
NOTE: the `ip` value is a LITERAL tailnet IPv4 (NOT a Jinja var reference).
Ansible's group_vars loader treats YAML scalars as-is (no second Jinja pass);
if `ip` were `{{ tailnet_sidecar_ip }}` it would render as the literal string
`{{ tailnet_sidecar_ip }}` in the headscale config, NOT the variable's value.
The deploy step MUST keep each per-sub IP in sync with the corresponding
`tailnet_<svc>_ip` group_var; today every entry omits `ip` -> all resolve to
tailnet_sidecar_ip = 100.64.0.1 (vps-obs edge).
Keep in sync with traefik-tailnet dynamic/routes.yml (obs edge) +
the sidecar compose templates (Pattern-A: dsh + pi-dev).
HD-405 (2026-09-20): MagicDNS records for the **`*.ts.kogler.si` namespace ONLY**.
This list exists because the one above renders BOTH namespaces (plain + `.ts`) — adding
`ha` there would repoint plain `ha.kogler.si` to a tailnet IP for every tailnet client,
which is the documented HD-382/389 resolver-ambiguity trap AND (worse here) would make a
tailnet-enabled phone at home stop resolving HA to the VIP, putting a new dependency on
oldsrv inside the failure domain HD-350's drill was about. `ip` defaults to
`tailnet_oldsrv_ip` (group_vars/all/main.yml), served by oldsrv's own edge.
HD-333 (internal all-app edge, Pkg F): WG-S2S reach for the internal edge.
The internal edge (`traefik-tailnet`, container) listens on :443 in its bridge
netns; host :443 belongs to the PUBLIC edge. The WG path therefore publishes the
internal edge on a DEDICATED port bound to the wg-s2s VPS address only, via
docker's compose `ports:` (host `{{ wg_s2s_vps.ip }}:{{ wg_internal_edge_port }}` ->
container 172.20.0.250:443). Docker's own PREROUTING DNAT translates host->container,
so NO manual nftables DNAT is required (same precedent as kopia-server :51515,
HD-62). An nftables input allow from the router peer (HD-313 pattern) is added
for defense-in-depth + spec compliance. `wg_internal_edge_port` is SSOT'd in
group_vars/all/main.yml (shared with the home `traefik-internal` edge templates on
oldsrv — HD-350): the traefik-tailnet compose, vps-hardening nftables and the
network-vpn.md spec stay in lockstep (derived-values ban: never re-type).
The internal-edge container IP on traefik-public (172.20.0.250, pinned HD-240).
Kept as a named SSOT var so the compose publish + nftables allow share one source
of truth; the /32 is stripped for the compose/docker host-facing bind.
